draft.title: Producers, consumers and decomposers
card: Producer
an organism that makes its own food using sunlight. Plants and algae are producers.
Consumer
an organism that cannot make its own food, so it eats other organisms. Rabbits, eagles and humans are consumers.
Decomposer
an organism that breaks down dead plants and animals. Fungi and bacteria are decomposers.
Decomposers return nutrients from dead matter to the soil. Producers can then take up those nutrients.
draft.remember: Every living thing gets its food in one of three ways: making it, eating others, or breaking down the dead.

a.q: A mushroom grows on a fallen log and breaks it down. What is the mushroom's role in the ecosystem?
opts: Decomposer
Producer
Consumer of living plants
Consumer of living animals
a.why: A mushroom is a fungus, and it breaks down dead matter, so it is a decomposer. It is not a producer, because it does not make its own food using sunlight.
a.clue: Is the log alive or dead?

b.q: A farmer in Queensland notices that a paddock with no bacteria or fungi in the soil has dead leaves piling up and poor plant growth. Why would the plants grow poorly?
opts: Nutrients in the dead leaves are not returned to the soil
Plants cannot make food without bacteria in the soil
Consumers cannot eat the plants without fungi present
Dead leaves block the sunlight that plants use for food
b.why: Decomposers break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil, so without them the nutrients stay locked in the leaves. Plants still make food from sunlight, so the problem is not that they cannot make food.
b.clue: Think about where the nutrients in dead leaves end up.

b.best: Nutrients in the dead leaves are not returned to the soil

problems.detail: The remember line says every living thing fits exactly one of three feeding ways. The card does not make this claim, so the line sorts the ideas more neatly than the card does. It is also not strictly true: some producers do not use sunlight, and carnivorous plants both make food and eat animals.
"Every living thing" is an absolute claim, like "always", that the card does not support.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and have one clear answer. The remember line overstates the card by claiming every living thing fits neatly into one of three feeding ways; soften it to say most organisms fit one of these roles.
